Module jakarta.data
Package jakarta.data

Record Class Sort<T>

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
jakarta.data.Sort<T>
Type Parameters:
T - type of entity from which query results are obtained.
Record Components:
expression - an expression that computes a value by which to order results. Alternatively, null if property is supplied instead.
property - name of an entity attribute to order by. Alternatively, null if expression is supplied instead.
isAscending - whether ordering for this attribute is ascending (true) or descending (false).
ignoreCase - whether or not to request case insensitive ordering from a database with case sensitive collation.
nullOrdering - whether null values are ordered FIRST, LAST, or by the data store.
public record Sort<T>(@Nullable ComparableExpression<T,? extends Comparable<?>> expression, @Nullable String property, boolean isAscending, boolean ignoreCase, @Nonnull Sort.Nulls nullOrdering) extends Record

Requests sorting on a given entity attribute or expression.

An instance of Sort specifies a sorting criterion based on an entity attribute or an expression involving entity attributes, with a sorting direction and well-defined case sensitivity.

A query method of a repository may have a parameter or parameters of type Sort if its return type indicates that it may return multiple entities. Parameters of type Sort must occur after the method parameters representing regular parameters of the query itself.

A repository method parameter of type Order allows a variable number of Sort criteria. For example,


 Employee[] findByYearHired(int yearHired, Limit maxResults, Order<Employee> sortBy);

 ...
 highestPaidNewHires = employees.findByYearHired(Year.now().getValue(),
                                                 Limit.of(10),
                                                 Order.by(Sort.desc("salary"),
                                                          Sort.asc("lastName"),
                                                          Sort.asc("firstName")));

Alternatively, Order may be used in combination with the static metamodel to allow a variable number of typed Sort criteria. For example,


 highestPaidNewHires = employees.findByYearHired(Year.now().getValue(),
                                                 Limit.of(10),
                                                 Order.by(_Employee.salary.desc(),
                                                          _Employee.lastName.asc(),
                                                          _Employee.firstName.asc()));

When multiple sorting criteria are provided, sorting is lexicographic, with the precedence of a criterion depending on its position with the list of criteria.

A repository method may declare static sorting criteria using the OrderBy keyword or @OrderBy annotation, and also accept dynamic sorting criteria via its parameters. In this situation, the static sorting criteria are applied first, followed by any dynamic sorting criteria specified by instances of Sort.

In the example above, the matching employees are sorted first by salary from highest to lowest. Employees with the same salary are then sorted alphabetically by last name. Employees with the same salary and last name are then sorted alphabetically by first name.

A repository method throws DataException if the database is incapable of ordering the query results using the given sort criteria.

  • Constructor Details

    • Sort

      public Sort(@Nullable ComparableExpression<T,? extends Comparable<?>> expression, @Nullable String property, boolean isAscending, boolean ignoreCase, @Nonnull Sort.Nulls nullOrdering)

      Defines sort criteria for an entity attribute. For more descriptive code, use:

      • Sort.asc(attributeName) for ascending sort on an entity attribute.
      • Sort.asc(attributeName).nullsFirst() for ascending sort on an entity attribute, where null values are ordered first.
      • Sort.ascIgnoreCase(attributeName) for case insensitive ascending sort on an entity attribute.
      • Sort.ascIgnoreCase(attributeName).nullsFirst() for case insensitive ascending sort on an entity attribute, where null values are ordered first.
      • Sort.desc(attributeName) for descending sort on an entity attribute.
      • Sort.desc(attributeName).nullsLast() for descending sort on an entity attribute, where null values are ordered last.
      • Sort.descIgnoreCase(attributeName) for case insensitive descending sort on an entity attribute.
      • Sort.descIgnoreCase(attributeName).nullsLast() for case insensitive descending sort on an entity attribute, where null values are ordered last.
      Parameters:
      property - name of the entity attribute to order by.
      isAscending - whether ordering for this attribute is ascending (true) or descending (false).
      ignoreCase - whether or not to request case insensitive ordering from a database with case sensitive collation.
      nullOrdering - whether null values are ordered FIRST, LAST, or by the data store.
      Since:
      1.1

    • nullsFirst

      @Nonnull public Sort<T> nullsFirst()

      Returns an otherwise-equivalent sort that orders null values first. For example,

      
 page1 = customers.livingIn(country,
                            PageRequest.ofSize(50),
                            Order.by(_Customer.stateName.asc().nullsFirst(),
                                     _Customer.cityName.asc().nullsFirst(),
                                     _Customer.id.asc()));

      If the data store is a non-relational database that is not capable of ordering null values first, then repository methods to which this instance is supplied must raise IllegalArgumentException.

      Returns:
      a sort with nullOrdering set to Sort.Nulls.FIRST.
      Since:
      1.1

    • nullsLast

      @Nonnull public Sort<T> nullsLast()

      Returns an otherwise-equivalent sort that orders null values last. For example,

      
 page1 = products.namedLike(namePattern,
                            PageRequest.ofSize(25),
                            Order.by(_Product.price.desc().nullsLast(),
                                     _Product.name.asc(),
                                     _Product.id.asc()));

      If the data store is a non-relational database that is not capable of ordering null values last, then repository methods to which this instance is supplied must raise IllegalArgumentException.

      Returns:
      a sort with nullOrdering set to Sort.Nulls.LAST.
      Since:
      1.1
